chunks: Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Jamil ibn Darraj, from one of his companions, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), that he said:
When a man confesses upon himself for murder, he is killed if there are no witnesses against him. So if he retracts and says, 'I did not do it,' he is left alone and is not killed.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on executing someone who confesses to murder without witnesses?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the principle of 'iqrar' (self-confession) in Shia jurisprudence, establishing that a single valid confession suffices for capital punishment even without witnesses, reflecting the Hanafi and Shia view of its probative value. It further highlights the legal mechanism of 'raj'' (retraction), where the confessor may withdraw their statement prior to execution, thereby nullifying the hadd penalty. This ruling underscores the balance between judicial certainty derived from personal admission and the mercy afforded through the possibility of retraction before the penalty is carried out.

en.hubeali:
Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr,f rom Jameel Bin Darraj, from one of his companions, 
(It has been narrated) from one of the two<sup>asws</sup> (5<sup>th</sup> or 6<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>) having said:

‘When the man accepts upon himself with the murder, he would be killed if there do not happent to be witnessed. So if he were to retract (his confession), and says, ‘I did not do it’, he would be left alone and would not be killed’.
